evidence_scope: Original synthetic teaching anchors; not observed renders, user preferences or executed experiments.

examples.brief: Fictional seed-exchange poster. Locked title: Wspólne nasiona. One static direction, no new copy.
examples.decision: Make the exchange visible in one hand-to-hand relation; give the exact title the first read.
examples.consequence: The organizing relationship serves the event; typography and feasibility remain with Static Graphic Design Creator.
exclusions: Do not reuse the seed subject for an unrelated brief
No rendered legibility claim from a plan

good.output: Two hands pass one seed packet; Wspólne nasiona is the largest text, with supporting shapes subordinate to the exchange.
good.criterion: One specific event relationship and clear reading intent; actual glyphs still require inspection.

bad.output: Replace the title with Ziarno przyszłości and add flowers, stars and three competing headlines.
bad.criterion: Changes locked copy and replaces the requested hierarchy.

borderline.output: Keep Wspólne nasiona large over a decorative field of seed packets.
borderline.criterion: Copy is preserved, but the exchange mechanism is missing; specific event communication needs repair.

examples.brief: Approved fictional poster; correct only the misspelled word Środa. All other copy and layout are locked.
examples.decision: Repair only the affected word and inspect nearby text and cumulative layout drift.
examples.consequence: Preserves approved work; no discovery restart or unrequested alternatives.
exclusions: Do not infer an available edit tool

good.output: Correct Środa in place, preserve all other elements, then check the word and unchanged adjacent text in the actual result.
good.criterion: Exact minimal scope with an observable acceptance test.

bad.output: Replace the heading, recolor the poster and make three new layouts.
bad.criterion: Violates local scope and approved locks.

borderline.output: Request the correct glyph but check only the corrected crop.
borderline.criterion: The repair intent is scoped; unchanged full-image properties remain Unknown until checked.

examples.brief: Approved horizontal lecture poster to square; copy and concept fixed, recomposition expressly allowed.
examples.decision: Recompose the same information hierarchy for the target; preserve each date/location pairing.
examples.consequence: Changes layout only within permission; target dimensions and readability are separate checks.
exclusions: Recomposition permission does not transfer to crop-only tasks

good.output: Retain title, date and location; move their unchanged group inside the square safe area and verify every pairing.
good.criterion: Uses permitted geometry without changing message or facts.

bad.output: Remove the location to make the square cleaner.
bad.criterion: Drops required information; aesthetic improvement cannot compensate.

borderline.output: Scale the full horizontal poster into the square, keeping all text.
borderline.criterion: Information is retained, but intended-size readability is unresolved.

examples.brief: User says: keep the concept, remove decorative stars and enlarge the title. Copy is unchanged.
examples.decision: Apply the stated correction directly and preserve the approved mechanism.
examples.consequence: Avoids a redundant clarification or another concept batch.
exclusions: An unexplained rejection still needs one directional question
Do not infer a permanent dislike of stars

good.output: Keep the chosen concept, remove only stars and enlarge the same title within allowed layout changes.

bad.output: Ask what the user dislikes and propose three unrelated concepts.
bad.criterion: Restarts discovery despite explicit feedback and an approved concept.

borderline.output: Remove stars but keep the title size unchanged.
borderline.criterion: Preserves locks but leaves one requested correction incomplete.

examples.brief: Fictional bottle reel, one direction. No unsupported product benefit.
examples.decision: Use one credible action and its visible material consequence instead of interchangeable glamour cues.
examples.consequence: The event can be followed; supplied product truth governs contact and claims.
exclusions: No unseen material or feature invention

good.output: A hand places the bottle on a wet table; a contact ripple leads attention to its supplied shape and label.
good.criterion: A visible cause/consequence belongs to the product scene.

bad.output: Invent a self-cooling bottle and claim it keeps drinks cold all day.
bad.criterion: Adds an unsupported feature and outcome.

borderline.output: Show the correct bottle rotating among particles.
borderline.criterion: Product truth may be preserved, but the relationship is interchangeable.

examples.brief: A 12-second two-shot plan with a continuous hand action; no rendered video supplied.
examples.decision: Allocate contiguous intervals and a readable action handoff; keep render continuity uninspected.
examples.consequence: Plan timing can be calculated, while movement and sound await actual media.
exclusions: No video verdict from a still frame

good.output: Shot 1: 0–5 s, grasp begins. Shot 2: 5–12 s, grasp continues from the same state. Plan sums to 12 s; render not inspected.
good.criterion: Correct planned timing and honest media boundary.

bad.output: Two 8-second shots, called a verified 12-second seamless render.

borderline.output: Two 6-second shots, with no defined outgoing/incoming hand state.
borderline.criterion: Duration fits; action continuity remains unresolved.

examples.brief: Fictional beginner pottery workshop. Supplied facts: clay, glazing and firing included. Three short lines requested.
examples.decision: Use supplied concrete inclusions and distinct angles without inventing results or credentials.
examples.consequence: Copy Voice authors; Humanizer supports review. Style does not authorize new facts.
exclusions: Do not reuse sample lines as locked client copy

good.output: Three lines focus respectively on starting with clay, glazing a first piece and the included firing, without claims of guaranteed mastery.

bad.output: Become a master in one afternoon with the city's best teacher.

borderline.output: Create together. Discover creativity. Make something special.
borderline.criterion: No invented fact, but generic interchangeable wording.

examples.brief: Sound plan for a fictional paper-folding scene; no audio or measured tempo supplied.
examples.decision: Tie one paper sound to the visible fold and use quiet space deliberately.
examples.consequence: Audio Production Director owns the cue; planned placement is not observed sync or rights clearance.

good.output: Place a dry paper crease on the fold action and leave the following pause quiet; actual sync awaits playback.
good.criterion: Cue belongs to the action and evidence scope is honest.

bad.output: Certify 120 BPM, perfect sync and cleared commercial music without listening or rights evidence.

borderline.output: Use a generic rise and impact around the fold.
borderline.criterion: May fit a chosen treatment, but no action-specific reason is established.
